evals.name: b2b-saas-tier-1-from-scratch
evals.prompt: We're launching a new AI copilot feature in our HR SaaS product in 10 weeks. It's a major release. Can you build me a full GTM plan?
evals.expected_output: Full GTM plan in Markdown with all sections: go/no-go answers, Key Info with specific target market and NOT-for, tier decision (should be Tier 1 with reasoning), bundle decision, four checklist sections with owners and dates, rolling thunder plan. Goals must have numbers, not just verbs.

assertions.text: Plan includes the 5 go/no-go questions with yes/no answers and a launch recommendation
Key Info section has all six fields: Who (market), Who (team), What (stage), When, Where, Why
Key Info includes an explicit 'NOT for' line
Tier decision is stated with reasoning (not just 'Tier 1')
Bundle decision is explicit (standalone or bundled with what/why)
Checklist covers all four sections: Strategic Readiness, External Promotion, Sales Enablement, Internal Launch Communications
Goals include at least one specific number (e.g. '500 accounts in 90 days'), not just verbs
Rolling Thunder section is present with post-launch activities

evals.name: should-i-launch-back-end-refactor
evals.prompt: Our engineering team just finished a six-month rewrite of our back-end data pipeline. It's faster and more reliable but customers won't see any UI change. Should we do a product launch?
evals.expected_output: A clear NO recommendation. The response should walk through the 5 go/no-go questions and explain that most are 'no' for an invisible back-end change. It should suggest an internal all-hands celebration instead of a public launch, and note that tier is not a function of engineering effort.

assertions.text: Response recommends NOT doing a public launch
Response walks through the five yes/no questions explicitly
Response suggests an internal celebration or all-hands recognition instead
Response mentions that engineering effort does not determine launch tier

evals.name: bundle-12-small-features
evals.prompt: I have 12 small features shipping in the next quarter. Each one alone feels too small for a real launch. What should I do?
evals.expected_output: Recommend bundling. Walk through bundle criteria (shared theme, shared persona, calendar moment). Suggest bucketing the 12 into 1-3 themed bundles. Reference the SocialChorus 'Innovation Lab' example implicitly or by name. Suggest tying to a customer event if one is upcoming.

assertions.text: Response recommends bundling rather than 12 separate launches
Response names the bundle criteria: shared theme, shared persona, calendar moment
Response suggests bucketing the features into themed groups
Response suggests tying the bundle to an event or calendar moment
